title: The Claude Code Partnership Begins
body:
Semester break. A decision to approach the design more systematically - not just "try a change and see what happens," but a real methodology: incremental layers, isolated variables, documented decisions, living documents that survive between sessions.

Enter Claude Code as AI co-creator. The first session established the project infrastructure: `game-state/`, `docs/`, Typst rule sheets, feedback forms. All six baseline rules documents read, 8 interlocking systems identified, 16 open questions documented.

Three research threads ran: wizard-chess genre landscape (Onitama, War Chest, Tash-Kalar), competitive card fighters (BattleCon, Flesh and Blood, Yomi), and cognitive load in game design (3-5 variables per decision = sweet spot).

The first architecture decision: three directions proposed for the game's structural identity. Direction A (Streamlined Tactical Grid, Onitama model) chosen. Direction B rejected ("just another card game"). Perfect information confirmed as non-negotiable.

Then the monolithic overhaul was proposed: change board size, HP, turn structure, economy, piece count, bodyguard simultaneously. Elias caught it: **"Don't change everything at once."** This became the mandatory incremental testing methodology.

body: Six custom Claude Code skills built (`/start`, `/wrapup`, `/research`, `/playtest`, `/scenario`, `/adr`). Discovery: skill directories must be unhyphenated.

title: Rules Audit & Typst Migration
body: All rule ambiguities resolved via explicit designer rulings: Rune timing (start of own turn), movement pathing (free route ≤ speed, blocked by all pieces), attack resolution (attacker stops before target if it survives), Bodyguard scope (Standard Attacks only), healing cap (none), Skill Path blockers (all pieces). Canonical baseline ruleset created in Typst. Build system established.

title: Playtest 2 Analysis
body: Full transcription and analysis of all materials. Layer 1 marked ACCEPTED. The standard attack dominance problem identified in the data: 2 DMG free vs. skill combos costing 3-6 Runes for equivalent damage. Skills are structurally the supporting act despite being the stated core fantasy.

title: Layer 2 Scrapped, Baseline Overhauled
body: The 3 HP proposal (Layer 2) was killed: first Champion kill was R26 with 2 HP - 3 HP would push that later. Guards at 2 HP vs Champions at 3 HP would create an artificial tier. Baseline ruleset rewritten with all Playtest 2 clarifications. `docs/backpocket.md` created.

title: Cleverness vs Attrition (The Turning Point)
body:
A full system-by-system audit revealed: the game consistently rewards attrition over clever play. Standard attack: 2 DMG, 0 Runes, infinite efficiency. Best skill combo in the game: 2 DMG, 6 Runes, 3 Skill Slots. The "best combo" merely matches what a free attack does.

Research on cooperative feel in competitive games found "mutual epistemic exploration" - both players co-interpreting the same puzzle. This was already happening naturally in Playtest 2.

Five design principles established (now in `docs/design-principles.md`). Layer 2 redefined: standard attack nerf (1 DMG) + multi-Champion combo bonus. Two-game test format: Game 1 tests nerf alone, Game 2 adds combo bonus. Rule sheets written, feedback forms created, all 15 skill icons added.

title: Playtest 3 Analysed - Stack A G1 Confirmed
body: Transcribed and analysed Playtest 3 (Elias vs Mario 17.05.26, Stack A Game 1: standard attack nerfed to 1 DMG). Key findings: standoff dissolved (first Champion kill R11 vs P2's R26), Bodyguard activated organically without the Stack B adjacency fix (may obsolete Stack B), Armor / Armor-Breaker RPS loop functioned as designed, and a cross-piece Move-into-Strike combo (Air Blast → Hook Pull) emerged organically without the combo-bonus layer. **Standard attack 1 DMG accepted into baseline.** Two new design questions raised as OQ-52 (centre-of-board has no attractor - flank-drift, cramped opening, King stays back) and OQ-53 (attrition vs regicide - King is currently incidental, not a target). Reframed Rune Theft (OQ-34) into Mode A (opponent at 0 Runes = normal Strike) vs Mode B (cheap damage + disable, time-dependent); P3 burst was Mode A, not dominance. Four new backpocket entries: 8×10 narrower board, starting-formation swap to expose King, "spec the game for a programmer" exercise (with note to research requirements engineering first), and digital playtest prototype (sleep-on-it, ADR required). Major ruling: Focus Strike on Move skills lets the caster choose, at activation, whether the +1 applies to activation range OR effect range (not both). Documented in `baseline-sections.typ` (Skill Reference + Quick Reference), on every Move skill card, and in `mechanics-evaluated.md`. Resolves the ambiguity that surfaced while building the cards.

Lance Thrust effective Range 0 while Injured ruled "cannot fire" - the chained derivation from baseline rules IS the ruling, not ambiguity to be resolved. User correction: never reframe a derivation as "let's make a ruling - it already is one." Memory `feedback_baseline_is_authoritative.md` written. OQ-54 (Lance Thrust wording rewrite) closed: keep "Range−1" - the modifier preserves a real interaction the "Adjacent" rewrite would obscure.

Decision logged for 2026-05-28: Niko plays the standard baseline draft. No starter loadout, no simplified pool, no rule changes for first-time players. Onboarding data comes from the new form, not from changing the game. Memory `project_niko_first_game.md`.

title: Digital Prototype PWA + iOS Touch Fix
body:
Built and deployed a single-file offline PWA prototype at GitHub Pages (repo made public). The prototype covers the full game loop: 10×10 board with drag-and-drop piece movement, piece state tracking (armor pips, injured dot, 2 skill slots with icons), rune tracking per player, end-turn notes panel, post-game feedback form (multi-select scale questions + notes), and JSON export per game. All 15 skill icons are base64-embedded so the file runs fully offline once cached. Board and all piece content scale dynamically via `--cell` CSS custom property.

iOS touch handling was broken (instant drag on any touch, modal unreachable). Rewrote from Touch Events API to Pointer Events API: event delegation on `#board` via `pointerdown`, `setPointerCapture` for reliable routing, combined 10px distance + 100ms time threshold before committing to drag, `requestAnimationFrame` wrapping for iOS 17.4 DOM repaint compatibility, and `elementFromPoint` with `pointer-events:none` on the drag clone for accurate hit-testing. User confirmed it works on iPad.

title: Playtest 4 - Stack A G2 + Niko's first game
body:
Niko (P1, first-time player) beat Elias (P2) on 2026-05-28 in a 28-29 round Stack A G2 game (~2h30). Elias surrendered on T29 after Niko's third consecutive Strike+Strike kill round.

Project-wide rename **Nico → Niko** (44 occurrences) executed first via sed: README, STATUS, OPEN_QUESTIONS, NEXT_STEPS, SESSION_LOG, HANDOVER, research docs, plus memory file and pointer in MEMORY.md. User finalised image transcriptions across 11 files in `playtest-results/elias-vs-niko-28_05_26/`. `/playtest` skill executed end-to-end with multi-agent isolation: two independent agents transcribed each player's materials separately to prevent cross-contamination of behavioural reads.

**Synthesis written**: `docs/research/playtest-4-analysis.md`. Combo bonus (OQ-38) **confirmed in mechanics**: Elias R11 margin "1. ever combo!!" (his first multi-Champion combo across all 4 playtests); Niko's R26-R28 = textbook 3-turn Strike+Strike kill loop (Blade Tempest + Rune Theft + Focus). **Weak in feel**: neither player rated the bonus "Very rewarding" - read it as a normal damage modifier. Cross-category crowd-out (Q-D3 risk) **partially confirmed** - Elias circled Rarely AND Never, Niko circled Sometimes. Bonus stays into baseline pending one more experienced-player game.

**Mid-game stalling returned despite Stack A nerf** - both players ran identical Armor-stack arcs (R15-R21 Niko / R15-R18 Elias), no Atk during the cluster. Elias D-notes: *"a lot of turns where we both didn't really know what to do."* OQ-11 / Q-C1 chassis-volume hypothesis received its **best evidence yet**: Elias Q13 "Yes, a lot" mental focus + game "Slowed noticeably" + verbatim *"armor was a part of combo calcs but it just felt like you were not able to do your combos because of it."* Niko's split read (Q13 "Not really" + "Slightly extended") suggests cost is asymmetric across skill levels.

**Stack H promoted to Priority 1.** Decision-tree literal output was Stack F (standoff persists), but the standoff observed is *Armor-driven mid-game stalling*, not opening-engagement standoff that Stack F's sente skills target. Stack H's pre-condition test ("does combo bonus auto-resolve Q-C1?") returned NO - Niko's combos overran Armor only after a 7-round stall. Chassis volume is the lever.

**Q-D1 reading contaminated.** Elias did not honour the teacher-vocab-checklist commitment ("I just used the words to make it clear what the game is about"; pitch box: "explained a lot of my experience and good combos"). Niko's engine vocabulary ("combinations", "skill combos", "stacking of skills") may be borrowed. The ≥2/4 strong-signal threshold is NOT met by this session alone. **Process fix required before next first-timer session**: either pre-game initials per word OR read-rules-from-document protocol. Tracked in `NEXT_STEPS.md` as Priority 2.

Other findings: Niko's Q15 favourite moment - *"killing powerful champion by surprise and also stealing runes to prevent skills next turn"* - is exact cleverness-over-attrition language, ADR-003 Principle 4 landing for a first-time player. OQ-21 Bodyguard regressed to 0 triggers (covariate with stalling, not independent signal). OQ-19 not triggered (first Champion kill R13 < R20). OQ-41 closes - length problem is chassis volume, not damage nerf. OQ-34 Mode B confirmed dominant.

Cascade updates: OPEN_QUESTIONS.md (8 OQ verdicts), NEXT_STEPS.md (Stack H Priority 1, Q-D1 process fix Priority 2), mechanics-evaluated.md (combo bonus + Stack H evidence pointers), systems-and-mechanics.md (P4 evidence on Combat / Skill / Health-Armor sections), STATUS.md (re-entry update).

**Post-analysis design discussion (Session 22 second half).** Designer pushed back on the initial synthesis: combo-bonus Q3 softness ("Somewhat/Neutral", "Bit of both") is **design-aligned**, not a problem - the bonus is by design a few-times-a-game payoff, not "do or lose." The lever is **scope, not strength**. Walked through every analysis finding for designer reaction; multiple reframes landed:

- **#6 reframed**: Elias's late-game Blade Tempest spam was not a behavioural choice between "use the bonus loop" vs "single-Champ burst" - his Strike-equipped Champions were dead. *"I did not have any other attack champs left."* Structural offensive lockout, not preference.
- **Must-pick density softer than initial read**: Focus is equipped 1/2 across the army (not per-Champion); Armor 2/3 across the army. The catalogue pressure is per-loadout, not per-piece. Initial framing was overstated.
- **Q-D1 teacher-vocab-checklist deferred**, not made Priority 2. Lower-priority lever surfaced: skill names were shortened or replaced with natural words at the table - vocabulary barrier could be reduced by **renaming**, not just by stricter teaching. Bundled with Phase B naming pass.
- **"Don't know what to do" pattern decomposed** into two distinct windows: (a) early-game positioning (no Strike skills firing in opening - only Defense), and (b) post-mid-game-exchange endgame (after first big exchange, neither player knows how to convert position into win). Two sub-problems, not one.

**Dual-counter combo design drafted.** Replaces the simpler scope-widening (Option A, Move-into-Strike inclusion) with a richer mechanic: two parallel counters per turn - **target counter** (different friendly Champions hitting the same enemy target, current rule kept) plus **attacker counter** (same friendly Champion hitting different enemy targets). Both counters live in parallel; if a hit qualifies for both, both fire (intuitive stacking - rare in real play, reward when it lands). Multi-target skills (Blade Tempest) tick the counter on every hit piece, with a watch flag for OP rollback. Standard Attacks excluded from both counters. Scope widened to any skill that hits an enemy piece (not Strike-only). Justifications: cross-category crowd-out (#3), late-game offensive lockout (#6), and the **exchange-pit** mid-game pattern (one cluster, pieces taken one-by-one - attacker counter rewards distributing pressure across multiple fronts).

**Path A methodology decision.** Stack H ships first. Stack A G3 (dual-counter combo + widened scope) is queued behind it. Reason: incremental testing methodology requires changing one structural variable at a time. Combo scope and Armor volume both affect mid-game pacing; bundling them blurs the read. If Stack H trims Armor and the exchange-pit pattern persists, dual-counter is the targeted fix. If Stack H accidentally fixes the exchange-pit pattern (chassis volume was masking it), dual-counter may not be needed in this form. Designer agreed with the methodology argument: *"yes i agree that it is very complex, especially at the current game size so i agree we first lower the complexity of the game and then think about this."*

**Three new OQs opened (full text in `game-state/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`):**
- **OQ-58 - Mid-game stickiness / "exchange pit"**: once an exchange starts, all action concentrates in one cluster, pieces taken one-by-one. Watched under Stack H.
- **OQ-59 - Opening + endgame "don't know what to do" pattern**: 59a opening chassis-skew (no Strike skills firing in opening), 59b endgame conversion gap.
- **OQ-60 - Cognitive load**: real concern or acceptable? G4 guardrail watch - informs how complex Stack A G3 dual-counter can afford to be.

**Six new backpocket entries** (each with Justification Rule writeup): Combo Bonus Dual-Counter (Stack A G3), Plague skill (Mystic, Range 2, ~3 Runes, inflicts Injured ignoring Armor, no kill), Lucky/Star Strike (Mystic, target anywhere on board), Focus replacement ("any skill +1 Rune for +1 Range" baseline rule, removing the Focus skill), Lance Thrust + Rune Theft merge (single skill: 1 DMG + optional Rune steal), "Runes" rename candidate (Phase B bundle).

Cascade updates (second half): OPEN_QUESTIONS.md (OQ-38 reframe, OQ-11 designer note re Armor Breaker died early, OQ-12 must-pick softer note, OQ-58/59/60 added), backpocket.md (6 new entries), NEXT_STEPS.md (Priority 2 → Stack A G3 dual-counter gated on Stack H, teacher-vocab-checklist moved to deferred backlog, Recently Completed expanded with discussion outputs).

**TESTING_PLAN.typ rewritten (Session 22 third pass).** Designer flagged the doc's structure as confusing: ordering signals contradicted, gate logic scattered across three sections, Stack A G2 status stale, post-P4 routing missing, Stack A G3 unrepresented. Rewrite outcomes: stacks renamed for legibility (H = Armor Trim, A G3 = Dual-Counter Combo, K = Piece Count Reduction, F = Sente Skills) with letter IDs preserved as stable cross-reference keys; **Stack I dropped** (folded into Stack H as the smaller within-stack dose - rollback is contingency, not a separate stack); **Stack B withdrawn** (defender-only adjacency - P4 confirmed Bodyguard tracks standoff state, different solutions on the table even if Bodyguard remains broken post-Stack-H); **Stack K decoupled from Stack D** (K owns piece-count reduction; D owns board geometry - independent variables); **Stack F sequenced after Stack A G3** (both target the exchange-pit pattern via different mechanisms); state lifecycle introduced (Active / Queued / Dormant / Resolved - exactly one Active at a time); Phase 1/Phase 2 decision tree replaced with per-stack *Routing on result* blocks. Cascaded to OPEN_QUESTIONS.md (OQ-11 / OQ-21 / OQ-27 / OQ-1b cross-refs), mechanics-evaluated.md (Bodyguard adjacency moved to Withdrawn, Stack I rollback note collapsed, board-8x8 deferred row updated), NEXT_STEPS.md and STATUS.md (new stack names + dormant/withdrawn lists).

**Skill sweep.** Updated `/playtest` Step 5 (Decision Tree Routing → "Routing - Which Stack Next?", Active/Queued/Dormant/Resolved structure, per-stack routing rules); `/scenario` Step 5 (TESTING_PLAN section now requires placing the new stack in the appropriate state section with the per-stack required fields); `/wrapup` Step 2 TESTING_PLAN block (decision tree tables → state lifecycle moves + per-stack *Routing on result* updates). `/research` and `/adr` verified clean (no stack vocabulary).

title: Defense redesign + two-pole game framing
body:
Stack H re-discussion gate (set at Session 22 close) opened the session and quickly expanded into a defense + game-shape redesign. Three diagnoses for the late-game Armor problem were tested: (A) Rune curve too steep - **killed** by user (starving Runes removes skill tension); (B) HP magnitude too thin - **killed** by user (no 2-DMG skills exist; raising HP just shifts the bottleneck); (C) Armor's *shape* is wrong, functioning as a **late-game survival tax / mandatory upkeep** - **confirmed**. User verbatim: *"i 100% agree that armor is like the tax you have to pay."*

This crystallised a **two-pole framing** that becomes load-bearing for the project's near-term direction. **Pole A - pre-game-draft** = current game (with possible incremental fixes). **Pole B - per-turn-draft** = radical alternative where skills are added to pieces during play. Pole B mechanics locked: skills are *reusable while equipped* (not removed after use); 12-skill equipped cap per player (6 Champions × 2 slots); shared action slots between moving and drafting; no Rune-economy activation gate. Skill pool effectively infinite - the cap is the constraint.

**Stack L - Pole B Per-Turn-Draft Prototype** becomes the new Active stack, claiming the slot for the 3-week vacation digital-prototype window with Jonathan. **Stack H - Armor Trim** moves to Queued; the bundled dose remains the lead variant, and the "build cheaper than break" risk is bigger than originally framed. Two new design principles promoted: **(6) game length is itself a form of attrition** (long games burn attention budget before the interesting decisions); **(7) while core identity is unsettled, prefer fundamental shifts over variable tweaking** (conditional - once core settles, incremental methodology resumes primacy).

**Pole A draft determinism** raised as OQ-62: sequential drafting drives an "always better to react" pathology. Proposal: simultaneous-reveal drafting (both pick 2 at once, repeat). User accepts limited PI loss *only* in the pre-game window. **Cross-pole fixing methodology** raised as OQ-63: when a fix targets a problem in both poles, test once or per pole? User lean: per pole for cleanness; resolved on first encounter.

Cascade edits performed mid-session per user direction (no edits before plan approval): `docs/research/path-y-defense-redesign.md` written as the canonical writeup; `design-principles.md` (+2 principles, date bumped); `backpocket.md` (+3 entries - Armor diagnosis anchor, Armor-cap-by-round, Pole B one-turn-killer potential); `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` (+OQ-61/62/63, OQ-11 status updated to Queued); `TESTING_PLAN.typ` (Stack L Active; Stack H Queued; renumbered queued list); `baseline-sections.typ` (combo bonus migrated to baseline as `section-multi-champion-combo()`, BASELINE_VERSION → 2026-05-30, Quick Reference row added); `mechanics-evaluated.md` (combo migration row + new "Methodology / Design Decisions" section).

**Repo housekeeping.** Deleted `stack-b-guards/` (withdrawn Session 22, never played). Archived `stack-a-cleverness/` to `old-game-versions/archived-stacks/` (accepted into baseline). Switched all Typst imports from `../shared/...` to root-relative `/docs/test-scenarios/shared/...` form so files survive future folder moves - the build script already passes `--root $PROJECT_ROOT`. Cleanup sweep updated WHAT_TO_PRINT.md, README.md, HANDOVER.md, scenario skill, baseline-sections docstring.

**Next action:** run the first Pole B per-turn-draft prototype game digitally during the 3-week vacation window. After 2–3 games, compare game-feel vs Pole A and route per Stack L's *Routing on result*.

title: Pole B rules + project-wide vocabulary + template redesign
body:
Three sequential goals tackled. **(1) Project-wide vocabulary simplification.** Broad rename pass across top-level docs, design-principles, systems, backpocket, mechanics-evaluated, research files, game-state, images README, skill files, and Typst rule sheets - 6 commits. Aligns terminology between files and removes jargon for both the designer and new players.

**(2) Pole B rule sheet written.** Standalone rule sheet for Stack L now lives at `docs/test-scenarios/stack-l-per-turn-draft/stack-l-per-turn-draft.typ/.pdf`. Fully inline (does not reference `baseline-sections.typ`) so the prototype reads as its own ruleset. Vocabulary: "Build Phase" → "Draft Phase". Three-phase turn: *Move Phase → Draft Phase → Skill Phase*. Move and Draft share a 4-action pool; Skill Phase is free with consumable activations (drafted skills exhaust on activation and return to the shared pool). Bodyguard sits between Move Phase and Draft Phase. Backpocket entries added for the three obvious Pole B variants - skills-cost-a-resource, per-Skill-Phase activation cap, permanently-equipped (non-consumable) drafted skills.

Canonical `shared/template.typ` rebuilt with merged choices: H1 = 28pt Inter Display title (eyebrow dropped - was static "Rule sheet"); H2 = numbered presence (big numeral + "SECTION" eyebrow + bold title) with calmer teal numerals so headings support rather than dominate the rules; H3 = small-caps teal eyebrow; tables = cool grey header + charcoal hairline + light alt rows; new `sk("Lance")` chip helper for in-text skill references - light tinted pill with category-color outline + visible icon, vertically centered; callouts = note (teal) / changed (amber, no longer red) / designer (muted grey).

title: Playtest 5 (Pole B digital) + Pole A revival as Active track
body:
User returned from holiday with P5 in hand: Elias (P1) vs Jonathan (P2) on the digital Pole B per-turn-draft prototype. Jonathan won after 15 rounds; first Guard kill ~R7, first Champion kill ~R9-10. **No exported game log** - Jonathan refreshed the browser and the digital prototype had no persistence, wiping all state. Insights captured at `playtest-results/elias-vs-jonathan-pole-b-digital-2026-06/notes.md` from designer recall plus mid-game reasoning.

**Three structural problems surfaced in Pole B**, and together they pause Pole B as the Active track:

1. **Armor 3 still felt mandatory cross-pole** - Jonathan flagged unprompted that "3 armor ist zu viel". OQ-11 chassis-volume hypothesis gets a *cross-pole confirmation*: the Armor problem survives the radical structural switch from pre-game-draft to per-turn-draft, which says the issue lives in the Armor numbers themselves, not in Pole A's compounding-stack dynamic. OQ-11 graduates from "Pole-A symptom" to "load-bearing across both poles."
2. **Play collapsed to pure reaction.** Per-turn drafting removed the multi-turn planning horizon: you can't plan a 3-turn combo when your future skill set is decided turn-by-turn. The engine that powers cleverness-over-attrition (ADR-003 / Principle 4) needs forward planning to fire, and Pole B's structure starved it.
3. **Felt-PI broke even though formal-PI held.** Both players had full information access (open boards, visible skill pool, no hidden state) but the *combinatorial breadth* of per-turn skill choice was too wide to internalise - neither player could meaningfully evaluate "what will the opponent do next turn given their full possible draft set." Formal Perfect Information was preserved; the *feel* of PI was not. New OQ-64 captures this distinction as a design-time smell-test for any future option-space expansion.

**Trade-off read.** Pole B replaced one problem (Pole A's draft-determinism + compounding-Armor late-game tax) with another (felt-PI breakdown + reactive-only play). It is *not* a net win, and going further down Pole B without addressing the breadth problem would be a sunk-cost-driven move. Pole B is **paused, not killed** - other Pole B variants in `docs/backpocket.md` (permanently-equipped non-consumable, per-Skill-Phase activation cap, resource-cost-on-activation) may be revived if Pole A track stalls again.

**Designer call: return to Pole A with two concrete sub-goals.** Game short but empty (15 rounds, ~? wall-clock) reframed: shortness alone is not the goal - *short AND meaningful* is. Two sub-goals replace "fix Pole A's standoff" as the working frame:

- **Sub-goal A - Onboard new players better (OQ-65).** Pre-made loadouts: 2-3 curated starter sets per side. New players skip drafting and get a coherent kit; experienced players keep the full draft. Directly addresses OQ-56 Problem A (drafting cognitive load for first-timers) without the radical structural switch Pole B attempted.
- **Sub-goal B - Drastically shorten the game (OQ-66, Principle 6).** Target 30-60 minutes. Multi-lever pacing pass, not a single stack - Stack H Armor trim is the biggest lever; Stack K piece reduction and Stack D board geometry are secondary levers. Game-length measurement (rounds + wall-clock + first-Champion-kill round) becomes a tracked axis on every near-future stack, not a separate experiment.

**OQ-63 resolved on first encounter.** Cross-pole fixing methodology = **per-pole-revival**, not once-and-carry. Pole A and Pole B are different enough structurally that re-validation is required when a fix moves between them; the cost of testing twice is lower than the risk of a single read masking a pole-specific dynamic.

**OQ-62 (Pole A draft determinism) goes live again.** With Pole A back as Active, the simultaneous-reveal proposal returns to active status - and naturally couples to pre-made loadout selection (both players reveal loadout choices simultaneously). Likely bundled into the first Pole A onboarding stack rather than its own stack.

**Stack A G3 narrowing note.** On reflection (no fresh evidence - designer review), the **attacker counter** ("same friendly Champion hits different enemy targets → bonus on 2nd+ hit") felt too generous as drafted. Target counter scope-widening (any skill that hits an enemy piece counts) stays as-is. Narrow attacker counter at design time when Stack A G3 rule sheet is written.

**Cascade updates performed mid-session** (under explicit user direction "schreibe erstmal alle diese sachen in die orte in den docs"):
- `playtest-results/elias-vs-jonathan-pole-b-digital-2026-06/notes.md` - P5 record created from recall (no exported log)
- `docs/mechanics-log/mechanics-evaluated.md` - 2 new Methodology rows (Pole B prototype outcome → Pole A revival; cross-pole-first-encounter); Stack L moved to Withdrawn with paused-not-killed wording
- `game-state/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` - OQ-61 partially resolved (Pole A continues), OQ-63 resolved (per-pole-revival), OQ-11 cross-pole confirmation logged, OQ-62 reactivated, OQ-64/65/66 opened
- `docs/backpocket.md` - 3 new top entries (Pre-Made Loadouts, Game Length 30-60 min, Digital Prototype Persistence) + attacker-counter narrowing note appended to existing dual-counter entry
- `game-state/NEXT_STEPS.md` - full restructure: Priority 1 = Pole A revival (two sub-goals); Priority 2 = Stack H promoted; Stack L → Dormant + Withdrawn
- `game-state/STATUS.md` - rewritten for Session 25; top-5 OQs = OQ-65, OQ-66, OQ-11, OQ-64, OQ-62
- `docs/test-scenarios/TESTING_PLAN.typ` - Active = "Stack TBD - Pole A Revival" placeholder with three candidate next-Active options; Q1 = Stack H (promoted, cross-pole confirmed); Stack L → Dormant (paused, with revival triggers) + Resolved row

**Tooling flag.** Any future digital playtest (Pole B revival, or Pole A digital) must persist state - auto-save per turn, export-as-JSON/PDF available at any time, per-turn state log. Until persistence ships, default back to paper for any "this game matters" run.

**Next action:** Decide on the next Active stack for the Pole A revival track - pre-made loadouts stack (OQ-65) OR Stack H - Armor Trim (OQ-11 + OQ-66) OR a bundled stack. User flagged that more holiday insights are still coming, so the next Active stack is NOT yet locked.

**Mid-session continuation - post-P5 brainstorm batch 1 (the path to the Game Length Cut).** After the P5 cascade landed, user shared a structured brainstorm dump covering 14 threads of post-game reflection (each annotated with "asan" - after sleeping a night). Most threads converged on a single conclusion: the next stack is a **Game Length Cut (GLC)** - a bundled change that compresses the game to the 30-60 min target while simultaneously reshaping end conditions to deliver a single-climax game shape (no up-down-up-down, no decided-but-still-playing tail).

The brainstorm chain (parked in full in `docs/backpocket.md` → "Session 25 Brainstorm - Post-P5 Direction-Setting"): (1) does the game need Perfect Information? - parked behind GLC; (2) would smart fair luck help? - parked, no justification; (3) win condition: King vs piece-count - folded into the GLC end-condition work; (4) HP/Armor power curve problem - parked, may dissolve with shorter games; (5) Armor as "easy progressive escape" - parked, re-check post-GLC; (6) Go-comparison on impact density (few high-impact moves punish small mistakes too hard; "≤1 min reachable / 10 min rewarded" KPI proposed) - parked; (7) what are players competing on? - parked; (8) Money's purpose is thin - explicitly NOT pursued now (would violate Principle 7); (9) **game economy / component map** - designer flagged as the next output coming in this session; (10) early-game pacing - leave as-is; (11) **single-climax game shape** - promoted to Principle 8; (12) Bodyguard removal - opened as OQ-67 (low prio); (13) draw conditions - opened as OQ-68 (gated into GLC bundle); (14) multi-Champ combo widening to non-Strike - folded into the GLC bundle (overrides the standalone Stack A G3 sequencing - to be reconciled when GLC stack is drafted).

**Principle 8 promoted to `design-principles.md`** - *"The game shape is a single climax, not a sine wave."* Pairs with Principle 6 (game length as attrition): short games + single climax = the shape now being optimized for. Practical consequence: end conditions must be reachable *at* the climax, not 10 turns after; game-shape becomes a tracked KPI in feedback forms.

**Cascade updates from brainstorm batch 1:**
- `docs/design-principles.md` - Principle 8 added; date bumped to 2026-06-21
- `docs/backpocket.md` - new top entry "Session 25 Brainstorm - Post-P5 Direction-Setting" with 14 enumerated threads (preserves the reasoning chain so future sessions see WHY GLC was chosen)
- `game-state/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` - OQ-67 (Bodyguard removal) and OQ-68 (draw conditions, GLC-bundled) opened

**Next action (updated):** designer's next output is the game economy / component map (the "übersicht" diagram). After that, the GLC stack will be drafted. More brainstorm batches still incoming - do not lock the GLC stack yet.

**Phase 3 continuation - economy map written + Stack M (GLC) drafted.** Designer shared 9 brainstorm images (`brainstorm-images/IMG_1083.jpg` through `IMG_1091.jpg`) covering the hand-mapped 12-economy overview, quantitative end-state numbers, stalling root cause, move-space combinatorics, win-condition alternatives, and skill brainstorm. Full transcription written to `docs/research/game-economy-map.md` - a reference snapshot covering: (1) the 12 economies (win, tile, health, armor, money, skills-available, action, piece-count, damage, piece-progression, movement, movement-variations-in-turn, +skill-variations-in-turn); (2) quantitative end-state at R1/R5/R10/R15/R20/R25 - tile occupation 0.24 vs chess 0.5, Money cumulative 6→109 over rounds, Armor theoretical max 72, max combo damage 65 cumulative by R15; (3) Insight #1 (Money is limiting until you have it, then actions are) → unified-action follow-up parked; (4) Insight #2 (damage > heal asymmetry → two-sided pathology) → not directly addressed in Stack M, watched; (5) Insight #3 (stalling root cause: piece-state-progression more attractive than board-action when board-action is too complex or unavailable) → structural argument for Stack M's combined cuts; (6) move-space combinatorics: ~2.2M end-to-end distinct moves in one mid-game position - quantitative footprint of OQ-64; (7) win-condition alternatives (reach other side / move King or specific piece to target tile / 50% Champion deaths) **parked as future direction, not adopted for Stack M** per designer call; (8) Injury debuff removal reasoning ("piece close to dying is already incentive to retreat; double-cripple forces save-vs-heal lose-lose"); (9) skill brainstorm IMG_1091 referenced only - out-of-scope, reserved for future skill catalogue expansion.

**Stack M - Game Length Cut drafted.** Rule sheet + feedback form at `docs/test-scenarios/stack-m-game-length-cut/` (PDFs built). Six bundled simultaneous changes:
1. Board 10×10 → **8×8**
2. Armor cap 3 → **2**
3. Injured state: penalties removed (still 2 HP tracker; no speed cap, no Range −1)
4. Draw conditions removed entirely (not replaced)
5. Steal cost 3 → **4** (both Modes)
6. Multi-Champion Combo Bonus also ticks on **movement-causing skills** (Tempest push, Hook pull, Blast push, Shove, Swap when relocating enemy). Move-Attacks and self-movement (Dash, Retreat) still excluded. Movement-only triggers tick the counter but deal no bonus damage.

Designer call verbatim on the bundling: *"alles auf einmal - ich will schnellen progress sehen ... das soll intetionally alles auf einmal gemacht werden, es ist mir egal das es gegen unser prinzip verstößt."* Stack M intentionally violates the Incremental Testing Methodology; the deviation is documented loud in the rule sheet's "Why we are running this bundled" section, justified by Principle 7 (fundamental shifts while core unsettled) and the schedule cost of 6+ sequential isolation stacks. Per-axis rollback routing provides surgical recovery: if length/shape/no-stalling all land → accept; if combo widening dominates → roll back movement-counter only; if length still too long without stalling → next is Stack K piece reduction; if cleverness gone → roll back combo OR Steal; if Injured feels disposable → roll back Injured only; if no-draws causes infinite games → restore only-Kings-remain. Methodology recovers on the next stack.

**Cascade updates from Phase 3:**
- `docs/research/game-economy-map.md` - created. Reference snapshot of designer's hand-mapped economies + quantitative end-state + 2.2M-move combinatorics + win-condition alternatives parked.
- `docs/test-scenarios/stack-m-game-length-cut/stack-m-game-length-cut.typ/.pdf` - rule sheet created. Uses `section-resource-economy()`, `section-skill-phase()`, `section-skill-system()` etc.; inlines the changed sections (Goal / Setup / Multi-Champion Combo Bonus / Health & Armor / Skill Reference) with `#changed-box` callouts; overrides quick-reference table for Armor, Injured penalty, Combo Bonus, Board, Draws, Steal cost.
- `docs/test-scenarios/stack-m-game-length-cut/stack-m-feedback.typ/.pdf` - feedback form created. 18 questions targeting game length, single-climax shape, stalling pattern, board size, Armor cap, Injured-no-penalty feel, no-draws environment, Steal cost 4, combo widening reception, per-turn complexity, plus standard systems + free-notes sections.
- `docs/test-scenarios/TESTING_PLAN.typ` - Active = Stack M (full bundled description, hypothesis, watching axes, routing, cross-refs); Q1 Stack H demoted to "absorbed into Stack M; isolation-fallback only".
- `game-state/STATUS.md` - current focus rewritten: Stack M drafted as new Active; Top-6 OQs re-ranked.
- `game-state/NEXT_STEPS.md` - Priority 1 = Stack M drafted; Stack H = absorbed (P2); Stack A G3 = post-Stack-M (P3); pre-made loadouts + Stack K + Stack J = post-M sequencing.
- `game-state/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` - OQ-68 resolved (removed via Stack M); OQ-11 / OQ-34 / OQ-38 / OQ-57 / OQ-66 marked "addressed/absorbed via Stack M, pending playtest result".

**Next action (final):** wait for next designer input. Stack M is print-ready. User flagged more brainstorm batches still incoming (*"ich habe danach noch weiter gebrainstormt, das teile ich aber erst danach"*) - these may amend Stack M before P6. Do NOT pursue tangential work.

title: Holiday-insights gathering + Stack M rule sheet finalised
body:
Designer returned from holiday with a backlog of post-P5 insights and the Stack M draft from Session 25 sitting open. Session worked in two layers. **Layer 1**: holiday-insights gathering - surfacing accumulated brainstorm threads not yet captured in living docs. **Layer 2**: Stack M rule sheet went through multiple correction passes. First pass identified two structural mistakes from Session 25's initial draft - missing onboarding sections (Introduction + Simple Overview) and wrong section order vs baseline. Second pass identified a stylistic problem - over-use of `changed-box` callouts (5 vs Stack G=2, Stack L=0) and diff-style "_(Baseline: X)_" annotations that made the sheet read as a changelog rather than a playable ruleset. Third pass took 10 specific issues from the designer: wrong numbers in Simple Overview (introduced when I called the baseline function instead of inlining); the Introduction's "What makes it deep" paragraph spoon-feeding the experience; setup piece placement (player does NOT choose tiles - Kings sit mid-back-row but not directly opposite each other, with a 2+3 Champion split and one Guard directly in front of each Champion+King); in-text skill mentions not using the `sk()` chip helper; a substantive design change to the combo bonus; the Skill System still containing baseline's "Injured Range penalty" text; Health & Armor over-explained; skill table Name column too wide; armor-cap annotations leaking into skill effect text; Facilitator Notes visible on the player-facing PDF.

**Substantive design change inside Stack M's combo bonus** (originated this session): bonus damage now applies to *any* skill - Strike OR movement-causing - that affects a target with counter > 0, not only Strike hits. This unlocks damage strategies without Strike skills, making movement skills a damage vector once a target is counter-loaded. Designer rationale verbatim: *"i mean, wenn du eine figur mit einem counter von 1 mit einem movement skill bewegst, dann sollte doch die figur auch diesen einen extra bonus damage nehmen, no? das würde es ermöglichen auch ohne strike skills damage zu machen, was mehr unility gibt für strategien und spieler."* This expands Stack M's combo widening from "movement skills tick the counter" (Session 25) to "movement skills also deal +counter bonus damage on a counter-loaded target." Quick Reference row and Skill System carve-out updated to match.

**Working norm reinforced**: when the designer raises a list of problems, *analyse first before fixing* - produce a diagnostic before touching code. Session ran the diagnostic step under explicit direction (*"du sollst als erstes selber sagen was du denkst die probleme bei den sektionen sind, sodass du erstmal verstehen kannst was der korrekte weg wäre bevor du ihn gehst"*) and that step caught the design intent of the combo bonus change correctly on the second read after a first miscoded fix.

Stack M PDF rebuilt clean; all 11 PDFs in the build script regenerated. No new OQs. No changes to mechanics-evaluated, design-principles, or backpocket - this session was a finalisation pass on existing work, not new ground.

title: Digital-first pivot + repository restructure
body:
*Digital-first pivot. Repository restructured. All design knowledge migrated into `design/design.db`.*

## The pivot

During the holiday, the designer decided that a "rumschieb simulator" (push-things-around simulator) is not enough. The deliverable in `game/` is now a **complete digital implementation of (GAME NAME)** with Stack M rules as the default. Multiplayer, AI opponent, multi-platform frontend (Desktop / Web / Mobile). The paper pipeline becomes a read-only archive; iteration moves to the digital layer.

Designer's directive (verbatim, German): *"ich will mehr mich in den digitalen prototypen lehnen. ich habe mich dazu entschieden im verlauf von meinem urlaub, dass ein 'rumschieb somulator' es nicht cuttet sondern ich eine komplette digitale umsetzung von meinem spiel haben will (aber die neu gemachten regeln von stack m als default)."*

title: Inspector core ships - entry points, tree, AI hint
body:
# Session 31 - Interactive Inspector core (`/inspector/`)

## What shipped

A new `/inspector/` route landed end-to-end with all four entry points the designer asked for:

1. **Paste a MatchLog JSON** - full game history reconstructed as a linear chain of nodes.
2. **Paste a FEN** - start from any position.
3. **Restore a tree JSON** - round-trip a prior exploration session.
4. **Fresh draft** - routes through `/setup/` (the inspector→draft→inspector loop is still incomplete; see deferred items).

The inspector is a true tree-of-positions, not a linear log. Each node carries cumulative `actions[]` from the start FEN, so any node can be replayed by the engine via a synthesized `Snapshot { start_fen, actions, config }`. Scrubbing back and playing a different move forks a new branch under the parent rather than overwriting history.

## UI surface

- **Tree panel** (left): DFS-rendered list of nodes with ply number + action notation. Points of interest section above the tree shows starred nodes as quick-jumps. Each row has POI mark/unmark buttons.
- **Board pane** (right): existing `Board.svelte` reused; click-to-move works for the Move phase (path picker + bodyguard chooser via the existing helpers). Skill phase uses an "all legal actions" list panel grouped by source square - radial wheel UX wasn't extracted from the 1485-line match page.
- **AI hint** (top of board pane): two buttons - `Ask AI (once)` runs a single search at the configured AI budget; `Search continuously` does proper iterative deepening (depth ratchets up by 1 per loop iteration, shared TT across calls, cancellable between depths, bails on forced mate). Banner shows best move + score + depth + an Apply button. The recommended action is starred in the legal-actions list.
- **HUD**: phase/side/actions-remaining string, End Phase button (during move phase), "Copy tree JSON" + "Play this position →" (handoff back to `/setup/` with the snapshot stashed in `match.pendingSnapshotJson`).

## Engine changes (Rust)

Added three new public entry points, threaded through wrapper_api → WASM + Tauri bindings → frontend `EngineClient` → worker + both clients:

- `request_ai_move_forced(m) -> StepResult` - runs the AI for the side to move regardless of seat kind, so HvH positions can be analysed. Falls back to a default `AiBudget` when the side has no AI configured.
- `request_ai_move_at_depth(m, max_depth) -> StepResult` - iterative deepening with no time bound, capped at `max_depth`. Caller drives the deepening loop and polls cancellation between calls. The match's shared transposition table makes successive depths progressively cheaper.

Inspector "Search continuously" calls `requestAiMoveAtDepth(d)` for d=1, 2, 3, ... up to a hard ceiling of 64.

## Bugs squashed mid-slice

- **`Cannot read properties of null (reading 'configJson')`** - `buildSnapshotForNode` deref'd a missing config. Added a `defaultConfigJson()` fallback that uses `match.side` when set, else seats both sides as humans. All four entry functions now validate shape explicitly.
- **`one row in the tree panel` rendered between rows** - `MoveListItem.svelte` had a leading `// …` line *outside* the `<script>` block; Svelte rendered it as template text. Removed.
- **`Ask AI` produced `NotAiTurn` error** - `request_ai_move` gates on seat kind, so HvH matches errored. Fixed by adding `request_ai_move_forced`.
- **Continuous AI restarted at depth 1 every iteration** instead of deepening. Fixed by adding the `at_depth` variant and having the JS loop drive `d += 1` per call.

## Deferred (captured in `next_steps`)

Seven follow-up rows added (priorities 20–28):

- **L6.7b** Top-K AI candidates (multi-PV) - open design choice between root-move evaluation vs. modifying alpha-beta root layer.
- **L6.7d** Preview window primitive (mini-board renderer for ±1 around a highlight).
- **L6.7c** AI search-tree viewer (needs Rust `SearchTracer` instrumentation; big slice).
- **L6.8** Skill tooltips - depends on L6.7d.
- **Inspector polish**: `/match/` HUD "Open in inspector" button, fresh-draft→inspector handoff, skill-phase radial wheel inside the inspector.
- **Inspector i18n**: hard-coded English throughout; needs `inspector.*` namespace in en.json + de.json.
- **Engine** exact-depth AI search (eliminate ID redundancy in continuous-search loop - perf only).
- **L6.9** Undo/redo + menu route (frontend).
- **L6.10** Polish + i18n + a11y pass (frontend).

## Verification

- `cd game/frontend && npm run check` → 0 errors, 0 warnings, 311 files.
- `cd game/frontend && npm run build` → built clean in ~4s.
- `cd game/frontend && npm run build:wasm` → WASM regenerated after each Rust signature change.
- `cd game/crates && cargo check -p core_engine -p tauri_wrapper` → clean.

End-to-end smoke testing in the browser confirmed (per designer): all four entry points work, tree branches correctly, "Ask AI (once)" returns recommendations on HvH positions, "Search continuously" climbs depth visibly until cancelled.

## Architectural notes for next session

- `EngineClient` is a singleton per app - inspector and match cannot both hold the engine at once. Treat navigation as ownership transfer (already works via the snapshot handoff field).
- The legal-action list panel in the inspector is intentionally redundant with click-to-move during the Move phase; the designer preferred having both available.
- Skill-phase wheel extraction is the main remaining UX gap inside the inspector. Either properly extract `lib/match/MatchInteraction.svelte` from `routes/match/+page.svelte` or copy-paste the wheel logic with a TODO. Decide at the start of the inspector-polish slice.

title: Match HUD export + in-game Sandbox mode
body:
# Session 32 - Match HUD export + in-game Sandbox mode

## What was decided

The live-match → inspector bridge is **deliberately removed** in favour of two cleaner affordances on the match HUD:

- **Export buttons** (Copy FEN, Copy MatchLog, Download MatchLog) - round-trip into the inspector via its existing paste entry points.
- **In-game Sandbox mode** - pulsing blue inset border, all moves apply normally (legal-action enumeration, AI hint, animations keep working), exit rolls back to the true position with a confirm-before-discard prompt.

This keeps `/inspector/` as a standalone analysis tool (the four paste/restore entry points) and `/match/` as a focused play surface with its own "what-if" affordance. The user explicitly wanted these two concepts kept apart.

## What changed in the codebase

Centralised action labelling (carried over from S31 close):
- New `src/lib/engine/action-label.ts` - single source of truth for `formatAction(raw)` and `formatSquare(sq)`. Handles Move-Attack approach squares, Bodyguard redirects (BG #N), Shove direction arrows (8-way compass), Focus retargets (shield/dash/retreat onto allies), Focus-effect 2-tile mode for Blast/Shove, generic `[focus]` activation-buff tag.
- Three call sites consolidated to use it: inspector legal-action picker, `MoveListItem.svelte` (tree edges), `AiHintBanner.svelte`.

Defensive fix for "tree has no configJson" runtime error:
- `inspector-store.svelte.ts:buildSnapshotForNode` now accepts a `fallbackConfigJson` and writes it back onto the tree to repair in-place. Both inspector call sites pass `defaultConfigJson()`. `loadTree` hardened to fail fast if pasted tree JSON lacks `configJson` field.

Match HUD export buttons + Sandbox mode (the main work this session):
- `match-store.svelte.ts` - added `trueSnapshotJson: string | null` + `sandboxMovesApplied: number`; reset in `resetMatchState`. `MatchMode` union extended with `"sandbox"`.
- `routes/match/+page.svelte` - three export buttons (`copyFen`, `copyMatchLog`, `downloadMatchLog`), `matchLogAvailable` flag refreshed on mount + after each apply, `showToast()` for 2.2s transient feedback. Sandbox `enterSandbox()` / `exitSandbox()` capture-then-restore via engine `snapshotJson` / `restoreFromSnapshot`. AI scheduler gated by `match.mode === "sandbox"` at the effect AND inside `runAiStep` (defence-in-depth). Move counter increments in the central `applyRaw` wrapper. Pulsing inset shadow via `main.sandbox-mode` class + `@keyframes sandbox-pulse`. `clearAllPickers()` invoked on both transitions. The old "Open in Inspector" button is deleted; `match.pendingSnapshotJson` field stays for the draft → match handoff still in use.
- `i18n/en.json` + `de.json` - keys `controls.copyFen|copyMatchLog|downloadMatchLog|sandbox|exitSandbox`, `toast.fenCopied|logCopied|logUnavailable|clipboardBlocked|logDownloaded`, `sandbox.confirmDiscard`.

## What this session did

No code changes. Pure design + research session, producing three linked plan documents in `design/inbox/digital/` that scope the next major work tranche (search-speed pass → NN evaluator).

## Outputs

Three companion docs, cross-linked, all in `design/inbox/digital/`:

1. **`nn-rater-plan.md`** - full scope for the NN position-rater (`next_steps id=25`). Headline decisions:
   - **Parallel evaluator, not replacement.** Hand-coded `evaluate()` stays. NN slots in via a new `Evaluator` trait. Multiple NN versions coexist.
   - **Path 3 (gradient descent on self-play labels) + perturbation injection** for local-minimum escape. Path 1 (pure mutation) and Path 2 (NEAT topology mutation) both rejected. Topology fixed; only weights move.
   - **Inputs raw, not derived.** No hand-engineered features - trust the net.
   - **Two-tier gauntlet selection:** cheap fitness filter against top-K of prior gen at 100 ms → full acceptance gauntlet (best-of-three mirrored at 100/300/500 ms vs every prior accepted version, ≥45% non-regression bar).
   - **Three champion tracks:** best-fast / best-slow / best-overall (slow weighted highest in overall).
   - **Training crate is native-only**, rayon-parallel for self-play. Autograd crate choice (`burn`/`candle`/`dfdx`) deferred to implementation.
   - **UI: opt-in observability.** Default = headless training at full speed. Local file polling IPC; UI never blocks training. Five panels (Live Match with three eval bars including hand-coded as control, Standings, Lineage Tree, Network Inspector, Gauntlet Matrix).
   - **No ADR required** - Path 3+perturbation is locked. ADR may still be written as record but is not blocking.
   - Pointer added to `next_steps id=25` body.

2. **`search-speed-benchmark-plan.md`** - benchmark infrastructure to grade optimisations before NN training begins. Reuses existing `Position::to_fen()` / `from_fen()`. Two modes (fixed depth + fixed time). 20-50-position hand-curated FEN corpus at `game/bench/corpus/`. Doubles as correctness regression test (≥1 known-result tactical position required). Manual run only, no CI. Termination condition: designer is happy with raw speed, then pivot to evaluator work.

3. **`alpha-beta-optimisation-catalogue.md`** - web-search-synthesised catalogue of techniques (chessprogramming wiki + Stockfish + amateur engine writeups). Nine categories: move ordering, pruning, extensions, quiescence, aspiration/PVS, TT refinements, ID refinements, parallelism, modern/less-known. Each technique annotated with expected Elo, complexity, correctness, and our-game-specific adaptation. Critical game-specific flags:
   - **NMP vs `EndPhase`**: `EndPhase` is NOT the null move (it advances state). Implement distinctly.

title: Quiescence Search + head-to-head match reveals evaluator bottleneck
body:
# Session 36 - QS implementation + evaluator-bottleneck finding

Goal: implement search speedups from the AB catalogue and grade them. Outcome: QS lands as a correct module but the grading protocol itself is invalidated when a head-to-head play match reveals the evaluator does not motivate piece movement.

## What shipped

- **Quiescence Search module** (`game/crates/core_engine/src/search/quiescence.rs`, new). Stand-pat + loud-action loop at depth-0 boundary. Catalogue §3 minus SEE. MAX_QS_PLY=8 hard cap. Loud = Move-Attacks + Strike skills (Lance/Hook/Break/Steal/Tempest) + Blast + BodyguardChoice. 380/380 tests pass including mate-distance invariance and `make`/`unmake` symmetry.
- **Bitboard `is_king_threatened`** (`quiescence.rs:105`). Replaced generator-based first cut (151% slower than baseline) with bitboard-fast scan + Chebyshev distance + skill cost/range gating (79% slower; lives with QS).
- **`DISABLE_QS` kill-switch** (`alpha_beta.rs`). `AtomicBool` flag, checked at `depth <= 0` boundary. Lets test harnesses A/B without recompiling.
- **`qs_match` example** (`game/crates/core_engine/examples/qs_match.rs`, new). Head-to-head match harness. Toggles QS per side per turn. Reports action-kind breakdown per game.

## What did not ship (and why)

Retested S36-rejected techniques (RFP, aspiration) on top of QS - both still failed multi-budget sweep:

- **RFP v1** (eval-gate): 6 score regressions at depth 6 vs QS-only, including reverting `midgame-low-skill-01` from -300 back to -750.
- **RFP v2** (QS-eval gate): identical regressions. Root cause - at gate nodes positions are already quiet, so QS stand-pats and returns the same noisy eval.
- **Aspiration windows** (δ=50, MIN_DEPTH=5, 4× exponential): +33% wall-clock at depth 6, no win. Re-search cost > window-narrowing benefit.

## The finding that changes the whole protocol

Ran a 3-game head-to-head match (QS vs no-QS, 1000 ms/move, sides swapped). Result: QS 1, base 0, 2 caps at 500-ply max. Action breakdown across 105 rounds: **0 skills cast**, dominated by EndPhase (80 consecutive in `aivai_demo` reproduction).

Root cause: `search/evaluator.rs` has no positional terms. Eval = material + HP + armor + skills + money. Move actions have Δeval=0 - the engine can not distinguish "Champion at f3 with Lance pointed at the King" from "Champion at h1 sleeping in the corner." Search finds no incentive to move pieces, so it spams EndPhase until the round-cap forces the next phase.

**This invalidates the whole search-optimisation grading protocol.** Every rejection in S36 (RFP, aspiration, PVS, LMP) was graded against an engine that does not play. "Depth-reached" was measuring the cost of searching nothing.

## Banked wins (kept even though grading protocol is invalid)

- QS module - correct under all unit tests, ready to grade once eval supports real play.
- Bitboard `is_king_threatened` - load-bearing primitive, will be reused.
- `DISABLE_QS` + `qs_match` harness - gives us a play-strength accept/reject path that is independent of corpus depth-reached.

## Next session focus

NN position-rater work per `design/inbox/digital/nn-rater-plan.md`. Eval is now the bottleneck for everything (search optimisation AND play strength). Once an NN-rater (or even a positional hand-eval) lands, re-run the full S36 sweep and the head-to-head match harness on top.

## Files touched

- new: `game/crates/core_engine/src/search/quiescence.rs`
- new: `game/crates/core_engine/examples/qs_match.rs`
- modified: `game/crates/core_engine/src/search.rs` (added `mod quiescence;`)
- modified: `game/crates/core_engine/src/search/alpha_beta.rs` (DISABLE_QS, depth-0 QS hook)
- modified: `design/inbox/digital/alpha-beta-optimisation-catalogue.md` (Session 37 retrospective appended; numbering in catalogue is one ahead of DB - catalogue "Session 36" = DB Session 35, catalogue "Session 37" = DB Session 36)

title: Backend flexibility + clean install/release pipeline
body:
## What shipped

Eight-commit infrastructure landing - no design changes, no rules changes,
no engine logic touched. End state: tag `v0.1.0` to cut a release; the
binary the user installs lets them pick CPU vs GPU at runtime from the
Training Observatory.

### Sub-slices

- **F1** - Repo cleanup. Deleted `archive/migrators/` (120K) and
  `archive/old-game-versions/` (17M); moved `archive/paper-pipeline/`
  → `design/raw/paper-pipeline-archive/`. CLAUDE.md / README / scenario
  skill updated to point at the new location.
- **A1** - `crates/nn_trainer/src/backend.rs` rewritten. Backend Cargo
  features became additive (vs mutually exclusive). New `BackendChoice`
  enum (`Cpu` / `Wgpu` / `Cuda`) with `available()` returning the
  compile-time set. `default = ["backend-ndarray", "backend-wgpu"]`.
- **A2** - `run_training` made generic over `B: AutodiffBackend`; a
  top-level dispatcher matches `BackendChoice` and monomorphises into
  the right backend. Cross-backend acceptance hop: GPU-trained candidate
  models are written via burn's wire-compatible `.mpk` recorder into
  `xfer-gen/` per generation and reloaded as `Mlp<NdArray>` for the CPU
  `NnEvaluator` (search-time inference stays CPU regardless of training
  backend - batch-1 dispatch overhead would dominate on GPU).
- **B1** - Tauri IPC: new `list_backends` command returning the
  compile-time-available set; `start_training_run` gains an optional
  `backend: String` argument parsed by `parse_backend_choice`.
  `tauri_wrapper/Cargo.toml` forwards the backend features to
  `nn_trainer`.
- **C1** - Training Observatory top-bar gains a Backend dropdown.
  Preselection is the build's default; last choice persists in
  localStorage. Tooltip notes inference is always CPU.
- **D1** - `.github/workflows/release.yml` - three-job matrix on
  `v*` tags: macOS arm64 (`.dmg`), Linux x86_64 (`.AppImage`), Linux
  x86_64 + CUDA (`.AppImage` from `tauri.cuda.conf.json` overlay).
- **E1** - Root README gains a Download section; `game/README.md` gains
  a backend feature matrix; new `CONTRIBUTING.md` covers branch
  convention, pre-PR checks, the slow-test caveat, release-cut steps.

### Architecture decisions worth remembering

- **Two binaries, not one.** `burn-cuda` v0.21 requires CUDA Toolkit 12.x
  at link time and won't compile on Mac, so the CUDA variant is its own
  AppImage built on a CUDA-equipped runner. The default binary bundles
  ndarray + wgpu (covers all Macs via Metal and any Linux/Windows with
  working GPU drivers).
- **Inference stays CPU.** `NnEvaluator` (search-time evaluator,
  gauntlet match play, inspector) loads through `InferenceBackend`
  (`NdArray<f32>`) regardless of which backend trained the rater. The
  `.mpk` recorder is wire-compatible, so the cross-backend hop is one
  save → load at the acceptance boundary.

- **CI is unproven.** The release workflow has never run. First tag
  (`v0.1.0-rc1`) is a dry run; expect to fix glob patterns / CUDA action
  pinning / Linux deps.
- **A3 integration test** - train one step on wgpu, save, load on
  ndarray, assert forward outputs match within tolerance. Deferred

title: Stabilisation - Cargo.lock pin, engine bug fixes, Linux fixes, RC2 release
body:
## What happened

Focused stabilisation session fixing issues surfaced by the RC2 release pipeline and multiplayer testing.

**Cargo.lock pinned.** CI was pulling `time v0.3.52` (released that day) which broke the `cookie` crate build (`Parsable::parse` signature changed). Committed `Cargo.lock` and removed it from `.gitignore`, pinning `time` to v0.3.51 (known-good). Fixes subsequent CI runs.

**Core engine bug - combo bonus self-grant on re-hook.** `tracked_enemies` stored squares, not piece identity. After `Hook` pulled a target to a new square, a second `Hook` from the same caster saw the moved piece as a fresh `(caster, target)` pair (no dedup bit set) and collected the combo bonus it built itself. Fix: `relocate_piece()` now updates `tracked_enemies` and `tracked_casters` when a moved piece is in either array, so dedup stays correct across all pull/push relocations (Hook, Shove, Tempest). Regression test added: `hook_same_caster_twice_no_combo_bonus_after_pull`.

**Linux fixes.** Three issues addressed:
- `WEBKIT_DISABLE_SANDBOX_THIS_IS_DANGEROUS=1`: fixes silent `AudioContext` failure caused by webkit2gtk bubblewrap sandbox blocking the PipeWire socket (WebKit bug #239682, unpatched upstream).
- `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1`: fixes CSS animation lag on wlroots compositors (Hyprland/Sway) where webkit2gtk DMABUF path fails to negotiate buffer formats.
- Multiplayer page: shows clear "not available on Linux" notice instead of cryptic PeerJS `BrowserIncompatible` error; webkit2gtk has no functional WebRTC backend (wry#85, open since 2020).
- Tauri bumped 2.11.3 → 2.11.4 (picks up official `time <0.3.52` pin).

**Bodyguard DTO fix.** The Tauri backend was serialising position snapshots without the `pending_bodyguard` slot, so the multiplayer match page never received it. Two symptoms: (a) defending player had no choice prompt to redirect a bodyguard intercept; (b) AI step-scheduler fired on the defender seat (no pending prompt → treated as normal AI turn), incorrectly resolving the bodyguard decision and dealing 1 damage to the attacker. Fix: added `PendingBodyguardDto` + populated from `api::pending_bodyguard` in `position_view`. `fen_to_position_view` always returns `None` (FEN encodes no mid-turn state).

**RC2 release pipeline.** `v0.1.0-rc2` tag pushed; two GH Actions runs succeeded after the Cargo.lock fix. All five matrix jobs (macOS, Linux, Linux-CUDA, Windows, Windows-CUDA) produced artefacts.

## Status at end

Multiplayer still used PeerJS/WebRTC (Linux excluded). Known next step: replace with a custom WS relay to fix Linux compatibility and avoid PeerJS reliability issues.

title: Multiplayer: WS relay transport + Fly.io deploy + v0.1.0 release
body:
## What happened

Complete replacement of the PeerJS/WebRTC multiplayer transport with a custom WebSocket relay.

**Motivation.** PeerJS/WebRTC was unreliable on Linux (webkit2gtk has no functional WebRTC backend, wry#85) and PeerJS itself had connectivity issues. A custom WS relay is simpler, cross-platform, and gives full control over the protocol.

**WS relay server.** New `game/relay/` directory; relay hosted on Fly.io at `boardgame-relay.fly.dev`. The relay is a lightweight message-passing server - clients connect via WS, messages are forwarded by room/slot.

**New transport layer (frontend).** PeerJS-based `transport.ts` (628 lines) deleted and replaced with:
- `websocket-transport.ts` (481 lines) - WS-backed transport implementing the same interface.
- `transport-config.ts` - selects transport based on `VITE_RELAY_URL` env var.
- `route-lifecycle.ts` - manages connect/disconnect lifecycle tied to SvelteKit route enter/exit.
- `MultiplayerStatusStrip.svelte` - new UI component showing connection state.

**Protocol trace documentation.** `game/PROTOCOL_TRACE.md` added (420 lines) - documents the full WS relay protocol message sequence for all scenarios (host create, guest join, move relay, rejoin, disconnect/reconnect).

**Release workflow update.** `release.yml` now injects `VITE_RELAY_URL` and `VITE_RELAY_HTTP_URL` secrets into the Tauri build so shipped binaries point at the Fly.io relay.

title: Task batch + Phase A/B search sweep
body:

Three commits landed since Session 40 end, all still on `main`. Treated as one working session per the user's note that "session" = a working stretch, not a strict calendar boundary.

### Commit `6eb2b03` - Session 41 batch (2026-07-04)

Grab-bag of UX and engine work.

- **Task 0 - Drop WASM entirely.** `wasm_wrapper` crate, `wasm-client.ts`, `worker.ts`, `build:wasm` step all removed. `engine/index.ts` unconditionally uses `TauriClient`. Simplifies boot + release pipeline. Rationale: Tauri became the only shipped surface; WASM path was dead weight and made the frontend engine boundary noisier.
- **Task 1 - Audio unlock after screen lock.** `visibilitychange` listener re-arms `AudioContext` on resume.
- **Task 2 - No spurious "abandoned" library rows.** Removed `pageHideHandler` + `onDestroy` fallback in `match/+page.svelte`. Natural end and explicit navigation are the only paths that finalise or abandon.
- **Task 3 - Sandbox undo stack.** Snapshot-JSON based, 50-entry cap.
- **Task 4 - Draft snap-to-nearest-slot.** Container `ondrop` picks closest slot by Euclidean distance; more forgiving on trackpads.
- **Task 5 - AI depth streaming.** New Tauri event `ai-depth-update` emitted per iterative-deepening iteration. `find_best_with_evaluator` takes `Option<&dyn Fn(u8, i32)>`. Frontend subscribes during `stepAi()` and updates `aiLastDepth`/`aiLastScore` live so the panel doesn't just sit blank while thinking.
- **Task 6 - Heuristic eval display in match.** New `heuristic_eval` Tauri command exposing `EvalBreakdown`. Polled after each move; `PlayerPanel` shows P1-POV score (signed for local seat). Guarded by `showHeuristicEval` setting.
- **Magic tables + evaluator overhaul.** `state/magic.rs` is now the single interface for board geometry: `movement_targets_speed1` (OnceLock precomputed 8-adjacent) and `movement_targets_speed2` (inline BFS-2 with blockers). `generator.rs::reachable()` refactored around the tables. `evaluator.rs` gained mobility scoring (Guards BFS-2, Champions 8-adj, rank advancement bonus) using the same helpers. `EvalBreakdown` extended with `mobility_p1`/`mobility_p2`.

### Commit `73afd8a` - Phase A cleanup (2026-07-04)

Groundwork before Phase B search optimisations.

- `magic.rs::cheby_dist(a,b)` backed by `OnceLock<[[u8;64];64]>`, replacing the inline `chebyshev_distance()` helper. O(1) table lookup.
- `generator.rs` refactor: all 13 call sites of local `eight_neighbours(sq)` replaced with `magic::movement_targets_speed1(sq).0` + a new `iter_bits(u64)` helper. Any/contains-style checks collapse to bitboard AND. `reachable()` attack loop delegates to `magic::movement_attack_targets_speed2` for both speeds. Deletes local `eight_neighbours()` and `chebyshev_distance()`.
- `make_unmake.rs::apply_tempest` neighbour walk uses `magic::movement_targets_speed1` with LSB-first bit iteration.
- Removed obsolete `_unused_player()` stub. Tightened `legal_draft_turns` to `pub(crate)`.
- Deleted `Match.started_at_unix_ms` field (written but never read since S36).
- **Bench baselines refreshed.** Old baselines were S36-vintage and predated the S41 evaluator mobility scoring; regenerated all 5 (`depth6`, `time100/500/1000/3000ms`). New baselines are the reference point for Phase B.
- All 392 core_engine tests pass; 20 pos × 10 runs determinism clean.

### Commit `b70c005` - Phase B search sweep (2026-07-05)

Ran the full Phase B optimisation sweep against corpus v2 atop the new positional evaluator.

- **B1 (NMP): ACCEPTED.** -9.4% depth-6 nodes, +0.27 plies at 1s, +18.6% NPS geom-mean, zero regressions at any budget.
- **B2 (delta prune in QS): REJECTED** at margins 2500 and 1500. Correctness drift on `combo-loaded-03` (score Δ=-118 at same depth) - eval is not material-dominated enough for the bound to be safe.
- **B3 (sort at d≥1 / d≥2): REJECTED.** Sort overhead at shallow nodes exceeded first-move-cutoff gains; d≥1 lost 0.33 mean plies at 500ms. Guard restored to d≥3 with an explanatory comment.
- **B4 (TT+killer promote only, no full sort): REJECTED.** Skill-phase-full bucket blew up +55% nodes / +58% time - history-based tail ordering is load-bearing where legal action counts are largest.

Also landed in the same commit:

- `tauri_wrapper/capabilities/default.json` - fixes AIvAI hang (grants `core:default` so `listen` for `ai-depth-update` works).
- `tauri-client.ts` - catch `listen` failures instead of throwing.
- Bench baselines regenerated with NMP=on.
- `design/inbox/digital/alpha-beta-optimisation-catalogue.md` + `game/bench/README.md` updated with Session 41 retrospective (corpus v2 provenance, per-budget acceptance criteria, why single-budget testing is insufficient).

## Status at end

- Engine has NMP-enabled search + positional evaluator with mobility scoring.
- WASM path is gone; Tauri is the only client surface.
- AI depth + heuristic eval stream live to the UI.
- Bench baselines are current reference for future search work.
- **v0.1.0 draft release from Session 40 has not yet been tested on prebuilt hardware.** Still the immediate blocker for publishing.

title: Stack N staging + repo/DB cleanup + design/RULES.md
body:
Two threads: a design pass that staged **Stack N**, and a structural **repo/DB cleanup**.

## Design - Stack N (Lethality & Standoff Pass), staged, awaiting P7

Diagnosed the P6 mid-game **"first-mover-loses" standoff** (oq-58) to a root cause: **ranged skill-kills are non-reciprocal** - unlike a chess capture (which plants you on the contested square), you kill from distance and pay no positional price; the victim loses the piece *and* the anchor. Aggression is positionally free.

Staged **stack-n** with three changes (all fold into `design/RULES.md`, marked ⧗ awaiting P7):
1. **Focus cost 1→2** (ns-32; two-source P6 signal).
2. **Max 1 move-attack/turn** (fixes early-Guard evaporation - a move-attack problem, not a skill problem).
3. **Strike-moves-caster** - after a Strike resolves, the caster steps 1 tile toward the target iff that tile is now empty (restores chess-like reciprocity).

Held in reserve: **Candidate X** (`bp-forward-guard-partial-skill-immunity`) - deploy only if Guards still evaporate. Candidate Y (opening development phase) and money-removal parked for future cycles. Both playtest bugs B1/B2 were already fixed last session.

title: ns-43 evaluator - 4 new terms, stage infra, per-position decider
body:
## What happened

Continued the digital-first AI work. **ns-42 (Stack N engine rules)** landed in this session lineage (commit `e3d4d8c`: Focus 1→2, max 1 move-attack/turn, strike-moves-caster + tests) - marked **done**. Then executed **ns-43 (parameterised, phase-aware evaluator)**: the term-registry framework (pass 1) was already committed; this session added the actual terms on top, one per commit, each self-play-measured and golden-guarded. ns-43 marked **done** (core delivered; tuner + perf split to new follow-ups).

## Eval terms added (all in `game/crates/core_engine/src/search/evaluator/`)

- **wasted_modifier** (Term 1, `f4dee0e`) - penalises a live Focus/Charge bit with no castable consumer in the Skill phase. Self-play noise-level, but closes a real blind spot: `useful_money` caps, so money burned on an unusable buff was invisible. Fires ~0% in self-play (rational search avoids the waste) - kept as a correctness hardening.
- **guard_isolation** (Term 2, `eb6594a`) - penalises a guard locally OUTNUMBERED (enemies-near − friendlies-near within radius 2). Encodes the designer's corrected diagnosis (bad guard was crammed among enemies, unsupported - not in open space). **56.2% self-play**, fires 50%.
- **champion movement-space** (Term 3a, `9f12544`) - rewrote the `mobility` champion branch from enemies-in-range (capped 60) to REAL reachable movement squares. **56.2%** vs the old coverage. Enemy-targeting moved out to Term 3b.
- **champion_threat** (Term 3b, `111be06`) - two symmetric soft-capped sub-scores: offensive (value-weighted enemy targets, strike-safety-scaled via step_toward landing square) + defensive (ally coverage weighted by vulnerability). 52.5% self-play (weak+/noise), fires 95% - prime tuning candidate.
- **endgame_closing** (Term 4, `13a1534`) - asymmetric, gated to the End stage: leader rewarded for king-pressure + escape-denial, trailer for king-safety + compactness. Correct + unit-tested, but self-play at 60ms/ply never reached the End stage (fired 0/425) so its A/B was uninformative. Stage threshold is the tuning knob.

## Supporting infra

- **Game-stage + advantage infra** (`ae7ab66`) in `EvalContext`: `advantage` (unified P1-POV lead = material+hp+armor+skills differential) + `stage` (Opening/Mid/End from on-board material with a round-number bias). Infra-only, no behavior change.
- **Determinism guard test** (`6f46fe7`) - pins the hard "same position → same score" requirement.
- **Per-position term-activation decider** (`53f1a5d`) - the designer's "activate only the terms that matter" idea turned out to be ALREADY WIRED (the `is_active(ctx)` hook: `evaluate_dyn` filters → runs only active terms → breakdown returns only those). Added behavior-preserving skips on the two costly/often-zero terms (champion_threat skipped when no champions; guard_isolation when no guards). ~2.3% eval speedup, golden byte-identical.
- **Perf: single-pass side scan** (`505b6fd`) - merged the two per-side material/value scans (~0.4%). Found the real eval cost is `champion_threat`'s ray tracing (algorithmic), not redundant work.

Every commit: golden test (byte-identical, or literals re-captured in-commit with rationale) + determinism test + `cargo test -p core_engine` + workspace check. Throwaway `search_bench` self-play A/B examples used for measurement then deleted. All on `main`, **not pushed** (12+ commits ahead, awaiting review).

## Deferred (new next_steps)

- **ns-44** - offline eval-param tuner (perturb `EvalParams`, self-play gauntlet). Prime targets: champion_threat weights + endgame_closing stage threshold + guard_iso depth.
- **ns-45** - convert `skill_attacks` (`magic.rs`) to true magic bitboards. `skill_attacks` is a classic 8-ray blocker-scan, not perfect-hash magic; converting speeds eval AND the move generator. Larger blast radius.
- **ns-46** - investigate search-depth futility (d12@30s ≈ d∞@1s). Mostly NOT eval - move ordering / quiescence / eval monotonicity. Possibly the highest-leverage AI fix; reshapes which eval terms matter.

## Not touched

No RULES.md change (eval reflects rules, does not set them). No push. No new playtests.

title: Ply-renderer visual fixes: strike-move, lunge to WAAPI, bodyguard animations + cover indicator (ns-40)
body:
## What happened

A frontend/board-visual session (no engine or rules changes). Fixed a chain of ply-renderer rendering bugs surfaced by Stack N, then landed the long-parked Bodyguard legibility indicator. All in `game/frontend/src/lib/`; `svelte-check` clean (435 files); full frontend vitest green (added 3 test files / ~20 cases). All on `main`, NOT pushed.

## Fixes (in order landed)

1. **Strike-moves-caster effect mispairing.** Stack N steps the caster 1 tile toward the target after a Strike. The renderer reconstructs skill effects from an identity-blind before/after mailbox diff (`diffSkillMailbox`), which mispaired the caster's forced step with the target's death/HP change - producing a HEAL glyph on the destination and a DEATH/damage glyph on the origin (point-blank kill). Fix: `extractCasterMove` pulls the caster's known `step_toward` step out of the diff and renders it as a pure relocation (dust + id-follow), never an impact. New `stepToward` mirrors engine `magic.rs`.

2. **Skill animations respect the caster's new end square.** Added `outcome.casterPostSq` to `SkillEffect` + a `casterAnchor(eff,size,t)` helper that interpolates the caster-end from origin to post-step square over the choreography. Wired into all five Strike renderers (Lance/Hook/Break/Steal/Tempest) so lines/coins/bursts track the sliding piece; spotlight moved to the post-square. (Designer picked "follow the piece / animate".)

3. **Move-attack lunge moved from CSS to WAAPI.** The CSS lunge never reliably played (speed-1 fired synchronously in the same flush as the state flip; CSS refuses to replay an identical animation string). Added `lungeReturnTo` to `PieceMotion` (mutually exclusive with `killLungeTo`): the attacker leans ~55% toward the target and recoils to its resting square via the same reliable WAAPI channel as walk/kill. Removed all CSS-lunge plumbing (`triggerLunge`, `lungeSquares` state/getter/interface, `lunge` prop + `@keyframes piece-lunge-1/2`, Board prop, both route consumers). Contact damage/SFX now fire at the uniform WAAPI peak. Designer confirmed the lunge finally plays. Fixes the "can't tell which of two adjacent attackers struck" UX gap.

4. **Bodyguard-choice animations.** A Move-Attack against a defended Champion/King is applied tentatively (no damage, `pendingBodyguard` set, side flips) and resolved by a separate BodyguardChoice ply - previously a silent `resyncFromEngine()`. Now: the attack ply stays SILENT when `pendingBodyguard` is set; the choice ply animates - DECLINE plays the attacker lunge at the target (+damage, or kill-lunge if it dies and steps in); ACCEPT plays the chosen Guard lunging toward the attacker and recoiling to its own tile (+damage on the guard, which may die). Threaded `preBodyguardPending` through `PreStateSnapshot`; damage/SFX at the lunge peak, board settle deferred by `RELOC_DELAY_MS` so the motion isn't wiped.
